title: The Kephalaia of the Teacher (excerpts, Sasanika Sources)
authors: Mani (Coptic Kephalaia); translation Iain Gardner
venue: Brill, 1995; excerpt PDF hosted at sites.uci.edu
ask_addressed: Roman law transmission (Gaius Institutes, Justinian's Digest/Institutes preface, rediscovery at Bologna), the spread of Christianity (Pliny to Trajan letter 10.96 on Christians in Bithynia c. 112 CE, Acts of the Apostles passages on mission routes, Edict of Milan, the Xi'an Nestorian Stele of 781 CE with its Syriac and Chinese text), Manichaeism's spread (Mani's Kephalaia or the Turfan fragments; Augustine's Confessions on Manichaeism).
quote: I crossed from the country of the Indians to the land of the Persians.
summary: Mani, speaking in the first person, says he preached 'the hope of life' in India, then returned to Persia, appeared before Shapur and was allowed to preach in Persia, Parthia, Adiabene and to the frontiers of the Roman provinces.
limits: The excerpt shows only the Sasanika selection; the chapter number is not printed in the excerpt and is not claimed here. The Coptic codex is a 5th-century translation of material set down after Mani's death (c. 270s), so the first-person voice is a later redaction. [Verifier] copy: unauthorised-looking upload; cite the publication, not this URL. The PDF is an excerpt of Gardner, The Kephalaia of the Teacher (Brill, 1995) hosted on a UCI course site. Strand lowered from documented to inferred and its years removed: the account is a later redaction with only relative dating on the page ('in the last years of Ardashir the king', 'the year Ardashir died'). Page text also names Parthia, Adiabene and the borders of the Roman provinces.

authors: Al-Biruni (quoting Mani); translator C. Edward Sachau

ask_addressed: Roman law transmission (Gaius Institutes, Justinian's Digest/Institutes preface, rediscovery at Bologna), the spread of Christianity (Pliny to Trajan letter 10.96 on Christians in Bithynia c. 112 CE, Acts of the Apostles passages on mission routes, Edict of Milan, the Xi'an Nestorian Stele of 781 CE with its Syriac and Chinese text), Manichaeism's spread (Mani's Kephalaia or the Turfan fragments; Augustine's Confessions on Manichaeism).
quote: they have been brought by the messenger, called Buddha, to India, in another by Zaradusht to Persia, in another by Jesus to the West.
summary: Al-Biruni quotes the opening of Mani's Shabuhragan, where Mani lists Buddha in India, Zoroaster in Persia and Jesus in the West before himself in Babylonia, the programme of a religion meant to be universal.
limits: Mani's text is known here through a quotation in Arabic by al-Biruni, written c. 1000, some 750 years later; Middle Persian Turfan fragments of the Shabuhragan exist (English Wikipedia 'Shabuhragan') but their wording was not opened.
